name: Translation-invariant Fluorescence Rendering via Fourier Convolution
definition: A rendering model where the image I is the convolution of a fluorophore density u_Λ with a translation-invariant Point Spread Function (PSF) h. It solves the problem of differentiable 3D image synthesis by moving convolution to Fourier space for efficiency.
summary: Translation-invariant Fluorescence Rendering via Fourier Convolution is a differentiable 3D synthesis method that models physical blurring by convolving fluorophore density with a Point Spread Function in the Fourier domain, enabling gradient-based optimization of sample geometry and optical parameters.
